text:
nina: Hey folks, I'm updating the region availability page and the localization team flagged ambiguous phrasing around where data may be routed. Want to align on wording + update SDK snippets (curl + ruby) before the next release.

omar: Agree. We should standardize on "routing preference" language and add a short FAQ entry about contractual residency. Compliance will need to OK the sentence.

lee: Also found a broken link in the Greek translation that points to the old endpoints matrix. Will fix but need the canonical link. Is it https://api.redwood.ai/endpoints or /regions?

compliance: Use the canonical endpoints matrix at https://redwood.ai/docs/endpoints (public). Important: avoid saying "stored in region X". Please use: "Requests are routed to preferred regional endpoints when available; guaranteed data residency requires a contractual agreement." I'll sign off on that.

nina: Thanks. Plan for the PR: 1) update wording to "routing preference" in top paragraph 2) add FAQ blurb 3) update curl and ruby SDK snippets to show `x-redwood-region` header 4) fix Greek link and add note for translators.

omar: For curl snippet I propose this minimal example (so copy/paste works):```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" 
  -H "authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" 
  -H "content-type: application/json" 
  -H "x-redwood-region: eu-west-1" 
  -d '{"prompt":"Hello"}'
```

lee: Ruby snippet for docs, showing header injection:```ruby
require 'net/http'
require 'uri'
uri = URI.parse("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate")
req = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri)
req['authorization'] = "Bearer #{ENV['REDWOOD_API_KEY']}"
req['content-type'] = 'application/json'
req['x-redwood-region'] = 'eu-west-1'
req.body = { prompt: 'Hello' }.to_json
res = Net::HTTP.start(uri.hostname, uri.port, use_ssl: true) { |http| http.request(req) }
puts res.body
```

nina: Great. Two extra asks: can we add a one-line caveat that private / on-prem deployments may ignore the header? And add the response header `x-redwood-routed-region` to the troubleshooting example.

compliance: Add this exact sentence under the top paragraph: "Setting a region header expresses a routing preference; guaranteed data residency is only available under specific contractual agreements." Approved.

omar: I'll add the `x-redwood-routed-region` example and a short CLI command for internal teams: `rwctl inspect <request-id>` to check routing. Make sure that CLI hints are marked internal.

preview-bot: docs preview: https://preview.docs.redwood.ai/branches/region-l10n-update (build 1342) :white_check_mark:

lee: Fixed Greek link and added note for translators: keep the region names untranslated (use canonical codes like `eu-west-1`). Also updated the translation key in crowdin: docs.region.routing_preference.

l10n-team: quick FYI to translators: do not translate the region codes or header name, keep `x-redwood-region` and `x-redwood-routed-region` verbatim. We'll push updated strings in the next sync.

nina: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4410 9 small change. Requesting reviews from @compliance @lee @omar. Will merge after preview build and compliance ack.

omar: After merge, follow-up sweep: grep for `X-Region` and `data residency` and open fixes for any stray pages. I can handle the grep and open follow-ups.

nina: Thanks all 44d. Planning to ship this with the next minor docs release.
